content_of_post_to_comment: Christians, help me think through this, especially if your first reaction is to disagree. We would never say repentance has nothing to do with God’s forgiveness of sin. But when we talk about forgiving each other, repentance suddenly becomes optional. So… if the way we forgive each other is supposed to reflect how God forgives us, I think my question is this: When people say, “you need to forgive even if they never repent,” is the thing we’re telling that person to do actually what Scripture means when it talks about forgiveness? How do you make sense of that?
comment: A distinction that may help: forgiveness as releasing vengeance and forgiveness as restored relationship may not require the same conditions. Perhaps Scripture speaks to both, but we often collapse them into one.
